THE FCC-MANUAL TECHNIQUE, discovered by necessity and now in VERIFIER step 1. fccid.io hosts the manufacturer's own filed user manual as a grant exhibit at a stable URL, reachable by WebFetch — no search budget, and it works when the vendor's site 403s you. A wave-9 agent that started with the budget already at 200/200 still produced two records this way, and the deciding fact in both came out of an FCC manual. Limit: no grant means no filed manual, so it helps most for exactly the connected devices whose tier is hardest to call. Note fccid.io's /search.php endpoint does NOT answer automated fetches — you need the grant ID, so get it from the vendor's compliance page or the product label.

D3 IS AT 3 OF 135, AND WAVE 9 LEARNED WHY IT STAYS LOW. The wave-8 index method (zigbee2mqtt.io, devices.esphome.io, OpenWrt's table, LocalTuya) still finds candidates efficiently — it just finds far more candidates than qualifiers, because most die on the physical-override trap. The rule to apply up front: for anything with a physical control surface — wall switches, dimmers, mapping robot vacuums — assume D2 and make the ESPHome project prove otherwise. Wave 9 established via an FCC-filed manual that the modern mapping-robovac architecture (Dreame/Trouver platform, and by extension most of the category) starts a full autonomous clean from a physical button with Wi-Fi setup as a separate optional step. That is D2, not a D3 lead. Look instead at devices with NO physical control surface at all — sensors, bulbs, plugs that are app-only by construction.

EASY D1 LEAD, probably the cheapest good record on this list: Martin Jerry's current RP-series switches (RP-S01/S02/SD01/ZB-S01/S02) ship PREFLASHED with Tasmota or Zigbee from the factory. A Wi-Fi wall switch that arrives speaking MQTT to a broker you run, with no vendor cloud anywhere, is a D1 as sold — no liberation needed. Surfaced while verifying martin-jerry-s01 (D2, the older cloud-bound model) and never followed up.
